resolved_findings.title: Freed active handle address reuse could retain retired execution payload
resolved_findings.detail: A live replacement handle reusing an old active handle address could satisfy pointer-and-scale equality. The stronger Rust active-payload ownership path then retained the old adapter. The original caller-lifetime rule excludes freeing active handles, but the Rust ownership extension needs a data-identity distinction.
resolved_findings.resolution: Worker added Arc::ptr_eq on live handle data before no-change return. Deterministic slot replacement test compares actual decode with separately loaded replacement and proves retired data released.
resolved_findings.status: Final formatted fix and test reviewed; implementing worker reports both native debug suites, strict Clippy, original-header debug clients and 226 + 4 export checks passed. Release validation was still running when this review refreshed.

conclusions: Weak handle-to-model references avoid a registry ownership cycle; model drop frees registered handles; manual free removes registry entry. Contexts retain base model strongly and active payloads through Arc, preventing dangling weights when the owning model handle or selected adapter handle is released.

Source first nonzero duplicate insertion, zero-scale skipping and count/identity/scale no-change predicate are preserved. Host-specific pointer-map order is measured by independent fixture traces; source operand order is retained.

Control-vector null disable, inclusive range, zero-length reactivation, complete-row updates and incomplete-row retention match frozen llama-adapter.cpp. State replacement follows successful composition and runtime validation, preserving old adapters/control/KV/output on errors.

LoRA ordinary and token embedding shapes, rank scaling and sequential application order agree with frozen source within admitted dense Llama paths. Tied-head embedding mismatch is explicitly rejected and documented.

Per-object metadata/tensor decoded+packed bounds precede matrix reads; execution-copy preflight precedes matrix cloning. Native adapter storage and rank-dependent scratch enter the existing work ledger; staged contexts share immutable Arc execution weights.
The Rust pretrained/execution fixture tests use actual metadata byte buffers and F32 words. Review inspected tests and retained source, not fresh execution of the 107-scenario final corpus.
qualifications: This refresh pins formatted source. Comparison against the prior reviewed fix found only whitespace plus an equivalent free-handle nested-if to let-chain rewrite; all other reviewed files retained their prior hashes.

The model 512 MiB aggregate limit is a retained-payload limit checked before publication; loading an incoming adapter and retained-control clones can precede aggregate/compose checks. It is not a simultaneous process allocation ceiling; documentation correctly distinguishes payload budgets from peak RSS and allocator overhead.
Live aligned caller buffers, correct lengths, exclusive context access and no stale-handle use remain required. The stronger payload lifetime does not make stale foreign pointer calls valid.
No release gate, full C ABI, complete scheduler or all-model claim follows from this source review.
